questions.question: Which of the following dates is correct with regard to the announcement of LPG model?

• Involves the transfer of ownership and management of public sector enterprises to private entities.
 
• It aimed at improving efficiency and productivity by bringing in private sector management practices.

questions.question: The ________ was abruptly called off by Mahatma Gandhi due to the Chauri Chaura incident.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-cooperation Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Non-cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920.
 
• It aimed at resisting British rule in India through non-violent means or "Ahimsa".
 
• The movement was called off by Gandhi in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, where a violent mob set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen.
 
• Gandhi believed that the movement had deviated from its non-violent path and needed to be paused to prevent further violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chauri Chaura Incident:**

 
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on February 4, 1922, in the Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces (modern-day Uttar Pradesh).
 
• During a protest against the British authorities, a group of non-cooperation movement supporters clashed with the police.
 
• The protesters set fire to the Chauri Chaura police station, resulting in the death of 22 policemen.
 
• This violent act prompted Gandhi to call off the Non-cooperation Movement, emphasizing that the movement must remain non-violent.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Movement:**
 
 
• Launched in 1918, the Kheda Movement was a peasant revolt against the British in the Kheda district of Gujarat.
 
• Farmers were demanding the suspension of revenue collection due to crop failure.
 
• It was led by Mahatma Gandhi, who helped the peasants in their civil disobedience struggle.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act Satyagraha:**
 
 
• In 1919, the Rowlatt Act was passed, which allowed the British government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial.
 
• Gandhi initiated a nationwide satyagraha against this act, which marked the beginning of widespread protests and hartals.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first satyagraha movement led by Gandhi in India.
 
• It was a farmer's uprising that took place in the Champaran district of Bihar, protesting against the oppressive policies of the British indigo planters.

questions.question: Torrential rain is any amount of rain that is considered especially heavy. Accordingly, which of the following Indian regions receives this type of rainfall during October and November?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southeast Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Southeast Karnataka experiences significant rainfall during the retreating monsoon season, which occurs in October and November.
 
• This region is affected by the northeast monsoon winds, which bring heavy rainfall during this period.
 
• The retreating monsoon, also known as the northeast monsoon, is characterized by the reversal of wind patterns.
 
• Regions in Southeast Karnataka, such as Bengaluru, receive substantial rainfall due to these climatic conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Torrential Rain**

 
 
• Torrential rain refers to extremely heavy rainfall that can lead to flooding and other natural calamities.
 
• It is usually associated with intense weather systems such as hurricanes, typhoons, or monsoons.
 
• In India, torrential rain is common during the monsoon season, which typically spans from June to September.
 
• The southwest monsoon is the primary rainy season for most of India, but the northeast monsoon contributes significantly to rainfall in southeastern regions.
 
 
 
• **Northeast Monsoon**
 
 
• The northeast monsoon, also known as the retreating monsoon, occurs when the monsoon winds change direction.
 
• It usually begins in October and lasts until December.
 
• This monsoon brings rain to the southern and southeastern parts of India, particularly Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka.
 
• The northeast monsoon is vital for the agriculture of these regions, as it provides essential water for crops.
 
 
 
• **Retreating Monsoon**
 
 
• The retreating monsoon is characterized by the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon winds.
 
• During this period, the winds change direction from southwest to northeast.
 
• This transition typically starts in October and marks the end of the primary monsoon season.
 
• The retreating monsoon brings significant rainfall to the southeastern coast of India, which is crucial for water reservoirs and agriculture.

questions.question:
Which of the following new words were added to Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act?

A. Socialist

B. Integrity

C. Fraternity

D. Secular

E. Equality
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 1976 during the Emergency in India.
 
• This amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The words "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity" were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by this amendment.
 
• The Preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and reflects its fundamental values and guiding principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socialist:**

 
 
• The term "Socialist" means that wealth generated in the country should be shared equally among all citizens and that the state should make efforts to reduce inequalities in income, status, and standards of living.
 
 
 
• **Secular:**
 
 
• The term "Secular" means that the state has no official religion and treats all religions equally. It ensures religious freedom for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Integrity:**
 
 
• Integrity refers to the unity and the sense of national solidarity among the citizens of India.
 
 
 
• **Preamble of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Preamble is a brief introductory statement that sets out the guiding purposes and principles of the Constitution.
 
• It reflects the vision and values of the Constitution makers and serves as a guiding light for its interpretation.

questions.question: Small scale industries in 1950 were defined as all those industries in which the maximum investment was ________ lakh rupees.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__ lakh rupees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1950, small scale industries were defined by the maximum investment limit in plant and machinery.
 
• The maximum investment limit for small scale industries was set at **five lakh rupees**.
 
• This definition was intended to encourage the growth and development of small scale industries in India.
 
• The investment limit has been revised multiple times over the years to keep up with inflation and economic changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Small Scale Industries (SSI)**

 
 
• Small Scale Industries are industrial undertakings having a fixed investment in plant and machinery, whether held on an ownership basis or by lease or by hire purchase, not exceeding a prescribed limit.
 
• SSIs play a crucial role in the economic development of a country due to their contribution to employment, production, and exports.
 
• The investment ceiling for SSIs has been revised over the years to reflect changes in economic conditions and industrial growth.
 
• In 1950, the investment limit was set at Rs. 5 lakh, but this limit has been raised periodically to accommodate changes in the economy and inflation.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of SSI Definition**
 
 
• In 1950: The maximum investment limit was Rs. 5 lakh.
 
• In 1966: The investment limit was raised to Rs. 7.5 lakh.
 
• In 1985: The investment limit was further raised to Rs. 35 lakh.
 
• In 1991: The investment limit was raised to Rs. 60 lakh.
 
• In 2006: The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act was enacted, which redefined the criteria for categorizing industries.
 
• As of now, the MSMED Act of 2006 classifies enterprises based on both investment in plant and machinery/equipment and annual turnover.
 
 
 
• **Importance of SSIs**
 
 
• SSIs are vital for economic growth as they provide large-scale employment and contribute significantly to GDP.
 
• They help in the utilization of local resources and promote balanced regional development.
 
• SSIs contribute to the export earnings of the country and help in the development of entrepreneurial skills among the population.
 
• They play a crucial role in the socio-economic development of the country by providing livelihood opportunities.

questions.question: What type of architecture was constructed in Hampi temples and palaces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The architecture of Hampi temples and palaces is primarily of **Dravidian style**.
 
• Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, and its architecture is a representation of the **rich heritage and cultural significance** of the Dravidian style.
 
• Dravidian architecture is characterized by **pyramid-shaped towers** known as Vimana, intricate carvings, and large temple complexes.
 
• The construction techniques and the grandeur of the Dravidian architecture in Hampi highlight the **importance and reverence of religion** during the Vijayanagara Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vesara Architecture**

 
 
• Vesara architecture is a hybrid style that combines features of both the Dravidian and Nagara architectural styles.
 
• It is primarily seen in the Deccan region, specifically in Karnataka.
 
• Examples of Vesara architecture include the temples built by the Chalukyas and Hoysalas.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga Architecture**
 
 
• Kalinga architecture is native to the present-day state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its Rekha Deula (tall structures with curvilinear spires), Pidha Deula (square-shaped structures), and Khakhara Deula (rectangular structures).
 
• Famous examples include the Sun Temple at Konark and the Jagannath Temple at Puri.
 
 
 
• **Nagara Architecture**
 
 
• Nagara architecture, also known as North Indian temple architecture, is characterized by its beehive-shaped towers called Shikharas.
 
• Temples in this style are generally built on raised platforms.
 
• Notable examples include the temples of Khajuraho and the Sun Temple at Modhera.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture**
 
 
• Dravidian architecture is native to the southern part of India, especially Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its pyramid-shaped towers called Vimanas, grand gateways called Gopurams, and large enclosures.
 
• Hampi, with its magnificent temples like the Virupaksha Temple, is a prime example of Dravidian architecture.

questions.question: When the total expenditure is less than total receipts, it is called ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**surplus budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A surplus budget occurs when a government's total receipts exceed its total expenditure.
 
• This situation indicates that the government has more income than it spends.
 
• A surplus budget can be used to pay off past debts, save for future expenses, or reduce the tax burden.
 
• It reflects a healthy financial state and efficient management of public funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balanced Budget**

 
 
• A balanced budget occurs when total receipts equal total expenditure.
 
• This indicates that the government is neither in surplus nor in deficit.
 
• Balanced budgets are often aimed at maintaining economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Deficit Budget**
 
 
• A deficit budget occurs when total expenditure exceeds total receipts.
 
• This indicates that the government is spending more than it earns.
 
• Deficit budgets are often used to stimulate economic growth during periods of recession.
 
 
 
• **Estimate Budget**
 
 
• An estimate budget is a projection of future receipts and expenditure.
 
• It is used as a planning tool to allocate resources effectively.

questions.question: Which species of Arthropods is horseshoe shaped, with hard shell and spine - like tail?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limulus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Limulus** is commonly known as the horseshoe crab.
 
• It has a distinctive **horseshoe-shaped carapace** that protects its body.
 
• It possesses a spine-like tail called a **telson**, which is used for flipping itself over if turned upside down.
 
• Limulus is a **marine arthropod** and is considered a living fossil, having existed for over 450 million years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropods**

 
 
• Arthropods are a diverse group of invertebrates that include insects, arachnids, myriapods, and crustaceans.
 
• They have a hard exoskeleton made of chitin, segmented bodies, and jointed appendages.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their ability to molt (shed their exoskeleton) as they grow.
 
• This phylum is the largest in the animal kingdom, with millions of species described.
 
 
 
• **Horseshoe Crab (Limulus)**
 
 
• Horseshoe crabs are more closely related to arachnids (spiders and scorpions) than to true crabs.
 
• They are known for their blue blood, which contains amebocytes used in the medical field to detect bacterial endotoxins.
 
• Horseshoe crabs play a crucial role in the ecosystem, serving as prey for various marine species and as a food source for migratory birds.
 
• Their spawning events are vital for the reproductive success of many shorebird species.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Horseshoe Crabs**
 
 
• Horseshoe crab blood is harvested for the Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) test, which ensures that medical equipment and vaccines are free from bacterial contamination.
 
• Conservation efforts are in place to protect horseshoe crab populations due to their ecological and biomedical importance.
 
• Despite their ancient lineage, horseshoe crabs are facing threats from habitat destruction, overharvesting for bait, and climate change.
 
• Research continues to explore the biology and conservation of these unique arthropods to ensure their survival.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for an Independent Election Commission for the superintendence, direction and control of the electoral roll and the conduct of elections in India ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 324**__.

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution provides for an Independent Election Commission for the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls and the conduct of elections.
 
• The Election Commission of India is a constitutionally autonomous body responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It ensures free and fair elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice President in India.
 
• Article 324 empowers the Election Commission to exercise its functions without interference from the executive or legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 320**

 
 
• Article 320 deals with the functions of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and the State Public Service Commissions (SPSC).
 
• The UPSC and SPSC are responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the States, respectively.
 
• They also advise the President and the Governors on matters related to the method of recruitment, principles for appointments, promotions, and transfers.
 
 
 
• **Article 323**
 
 
• Article 323 lays down provisions for Tribunals for adjudicating disputes and complaints with respect to the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts.
 
• It provides for the establishment of administrative tribunals for the Union and the States.
 
 
 
• **Article 329**
 
 
• Article 329 bars interference by courts in electoral matters.
 
• No election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State shall be called into question except by an election petition.
 
• It ensures the sanctity of the election process by prohibiting judicial intervention until the entire election process is completed.

questions.question: The first Indian Factories Act 1881 was mainly related to which subject?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Child labour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, a beginning in the regulation of child labour was made in 1881 when the first Factories Act was enacted.
 
• The act prohibited the employment of children less than 7 years of age in factories and
 
• It fixed their maximum hours of work at 9 hours a day.
 
• It also provided for a weekly holiday for children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Important Features of the Act

 
• Important definition under the act

 
 
• Child means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age.
 
• Establishment: includes a shop, commercial establishment, workshop, farm, residential hotel, restaurant, eating.
 
• Workshop: Any premises wherein any industrial process is carried on.
 
• Occupier: The person who has the ultimate control over the establishment or the workshop.
 
 
 
• The act under its schedule provides a list of employment. No child shall be employed or permitted to work in :

 
• Transport, catering or construction by railways, Mines, Foundries, Power loom, Cement Manufacture, Mica-cutting and splitting, Shellac Manufacture, Soap manufacture, Building and construction manufacturing of pesticides and insecticides, Papermaking, Oil refinery.
 
• Firecracker shop, Slaughterhouse, Manufacture of matches, explosives, and fireworks
 
• As domestic servants.
 
• Automobile workshop or garages.
 
• Dhabas, restaurants, hotels, motels, tea shops, resorts, spas, etc.
 
• Carpet weaving industry, Cloth printing, dyeing, and weaving.

 
• Power to amend the Schedule: The Central Government, after giving notification in the Official Gazette, not less than three months’ notice of its intention so to do, may add any occupation or process to the Schedule, and thereupon the Schedule shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly.
 
• Condition of work
 
 
• No child shall be required or permitted to work in excess hours.
 
• The period of work on each day so fixed that no period shall exceed three hours and that no child shall work for more than three hours before he has had an interval for rest for at least one hour.
 
• The period of work of a child shall not be spread over more than six hours, including interval time & the time spent in waiting for work.
 
• No child shall be permitted to work between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m.
 
• No child shall be permitted or required to work overtime.
 
• No child shall be permitted to work in any establishment on any day on which he has already been working in another establishment.
 
• Every child employed in an establishment shall be allowed in each week, a holiday or one whole day, which day shall be specified by the occupier in a notice permanently exhibited in a conspicuous place in the establishment.
 
 
 
• Labour Technical Advisory Committee:
 
 
• This committee shall advise the Central Government about the additions of any industry or occupations to exclude prohibit child employment.
 
• The Committee shall consist of Chairman and other members not exceeding in total ten.
 
• The Committee shall have the power to regulate its own procedure.
 
• The Committee may if it deems it necessary so to do, constitute one or more sub-committees.
 
• The term of the Child labour Technical Advisory Committee shall be one year which may be extended for two years.
 
• The officer not below the rank of undersecretary to the Government of India may be appointed as secretary of the Committee.
 
 
 
• Every occupier in relation to an establishment in which a child was employed, within a period of thirty days, send to the Inspector a written notice containing the following particulars
 
 
• The name and situation of the establishment;
 
• The name of the occupier;
 
• The address of the establishment;
 
• The nature of the occupation or process.
 
 
 
• The above provision does not apply to any workshop carried on by the occupier with the aid of his family.
 
• It is mandatory for every occupier to maintain a register for inspection by Inspector at all times during working hours containing information about the employers.
 
• In case of a dispute regarding the age of the child who is employed or permitted to work in the absence of a certificate of work, such a question may be referred to the prescribed medical authority.
 
• Whoever fails to give notice to Inspector shall be punished with simple imprisonment which may extend to one month or with fine or both.
 
• The appropriate Government shall make rules for child employment regarding:
 
 
• Cleanliness at the workplace; 
 
• Disposal of wastes and effluents;
 
• Ventilation and temperature;
 
• Dust and fume;
 
• Lighting and drinking water etc.
 
 
 
• Whoever employs any child in contravention of this act shall be punished with imprisonment or fine or both.

__
 
• Density of population

 
 
• The density of population refers to the ratio of the total population to the total geographical area of the country.
 
• With an average density of 382 persons per sq km in the year 2011, India is considered one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
 
 
 
• Types of density classes
 
 
• High-density districts
 
 
• The largest compact belt of high-density population spreads over the districts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Eastern and Southern Haryana, Punjab, and Delhi.
 
• The high density of the population is due to urban-industrial as well as agricultural development.
 
 
 
• Moderate-density districts
 
 
• These districts are found adjacent to the high-density districts in northern and eastern India.
 
• In peninsular India, moderate-density districts are found in Maharashtra, Gujarat, parts of Rayalseema and Telangana, coastal Andhra Pradesh, and some parts of Tamil Nadu.
 
• These areas have less fertile soil and a limited supply of freshwater as compared to the high-density districts.
 
 
 
• Low-density districts
 
 
• Low-density districts are characterized by physical constraints like hilly topography, scarcity of water, adverse climatic conditions, and dense forest areas.
 
• Most parts of Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and western Odisha belong to this class of districts.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Spatial distribution of India

 
 
• Areas of extremely low density: These are the areas having a population of up to 100 persons per sq km.
 
• Areas of low density: These areas have a population density of 101 to 270 persons per sq km.
 
• Areas of medium density: This class includes areas with a population of 271 to 600 persons per sq km.
 
• Areas of high density: These areas have a population density of 601 to 1,000 persons per sq km. 
 
• Areas of very high density: These are the areas with a population of more than 1000 persons per sq km.
 
 

Thus, the largest compact belt of high-density of the population in India has the regions of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Punjab, Delhi, and some parts of Haryana.

questions.question: Which of the following concepts refers to the income earned by the factors of production at factor cost in the form of wages, profits, rent, interest, etc., within the domestic territory of a country ?

options.text: Net Domestic Product at Market Prices
Net Domestic Product at Factor Cost
Gross Domestic Product at Market Prices
Gross National Product at Factor Cost

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net Domestic Product at Factor Cost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Factor Cost:

 
 
• Factor cost is the total production cost of goods and services, measured as the sum of the income earned by the factors of production (land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship).
 
• In simple terms, it is the cost of employing resources in producing goods and services, without considering any taxes or subsidies.
 
• Factor cost provides a perspective on the costs acquired by businesses in an economy to produce the goods and services that are consumed.
 
 
 
• Using the concepts of market price and factor cost, we can differentiate between NNP at Market prices and NNP at Factor cost:
 
• NNP (Net National Product) at Market Price:
 
 
• This is the value of final goods and services produced within an economy, including net income from abroad, measured at market prices. It includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies paid by the government.
 
• It is essentially the GDP (Gross Domestic Product) adjusted for depreciation and net factor income from abroad.
 
 
 
• NNP at Factor Cost:
 
 
• This is the value of final goods and services produced within the economy, including net income from abroad, measured at factor cost.
 
• To calculate NNP at factor cost, we deduct indirect taxes and add subsidies to the NNP at market price.
 
• This gives us a measure of the income generated by the factors of production, disregarding the taxes and subsidies that may affect the market price.
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• Suppose the NNP at market price for an economy is ₹1,000 billion (1 lakh crore), with indirect taxes of ₹100 billion (10,000 crores) and subsidies of ₹50 billion (5,000 crores). 
 
• To calculate the NNP at factor cost, we would subtract the indirect taxes (₹100 billion) and add the subsidies (₹50 billion) to the NNP at market price (₹1,000 billion).
 
• This results in an NNP at a factor cost of ₹950 billion (₹1,000 billion - ₹100 billion + ₹50 billion).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• NNP at factor cost, also known as Net National Income, represents the total income generated by an economy's factors of production, such as labour and capital.
 
• It measures the net value of goods and services produced within a nation and includes net income from abroad, measured at the cost of employing resources in production.
 
• By excluding the effects of indirect taxes and subsidies, it offers a clear assessment of the actual earnings of an economy's resources, reflecting the income available to its citizens.

• **Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs):**

 
 
• MLAs are elected representatives of the people in a state legislature.
 
• They are responsible for making laws for their respective states, representing the interests of their constituents, and participating in the legislative process.
 
• The number of MLAs in each state varies based on its population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Attorney General:**

 
 
• The Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• They represent the government in the Supreme Court of India and other courts.
 
• They provide legal advice to the government on various matters of law.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the Supreme Court of India, the highest judicial body in the country.
 
• They are responsible for the administration of the Supreme Court and preside over the proceedings of the court.
 
• They play a crucial role in upholding the Constitution and ensuring the independence of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of a High Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is the head of the High Court in a particular state or union territory.
 
• They are responsible for the administration of the High Court and preside over its proceedings.
 
• They play a vital role in the judicial system of their respective jurisdictions.

questions.question: Yamini Krishnamurthy, an eminent _________ and Bharatanatyam dancer has been awarded the Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Kuchipudi ** 

 
 
• One of the eight principal Indian classical dances is Kuchipudi.
 
• It comes from the Andhra Pradesh state of India, specifically the village of Kuchipudi.
 
• Kuchipudi was created as a way to worship Krishna, a Hindu deity.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi, a gifted poet and visionary who belonged to the Vaishnava sect and had the ability to give some of his visions solid form, created the Kuchipudi style of Yakshagaana in the 17th century.
 
• Kuchipudi is renowned for its dynamic storytelling, dramatic characterization, outstanding, rapid dancing, and expressive eye movements.
 
• Tandava (the regal, masculine) and Lasya (lyrical graceful and feminine energy) are combined in this dance.
 
• Other famous dance forms of Andhra Pradesh include - Vilasini Natyam, Andhra Natyam, Bhamakalpam, Veeranatyam, Dappu, Tappeta Gullu, Lambadi, Dhimsa, Kolattam, Butta Bommalu.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kathakali **

 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, a state in the southern part of India.
 
• It is distinguished by its vibrant costumes, elaborate makeup, and face masks that the performers wear.
 
• Kathakali translates to "Story-Play" and is known for its intricate storytelling, detailed gestures, and expressive eye movements.
 
• The dance form combines dance, music, drama, and literature into a composite art form, making it unique and complex.
 
• Themes of Kathakali are mostly taken from the Indian epics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and other ancient scriptures.
 
• It is performed exclusively by men and involves rigorous physical training to master the art form.
 
• The music used in Kathakali is called Sopanam and is sung in the Malayalam language.
 
 
 
• **Kathak **
 
 
• Kathak is a North Indian dance which originated in the state of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
• The name Kathak comes from the word "katha" which means a story. Shambhu Maharaj is one of the famous Kathak dancer.
 
 
 
• ​Sattriya
 
• Satriya Nritya is the classical dance form of Assam which represents the Satriya culture, the basis of the religious and cultural fabric of Assam__.
 
 
• It is a dance-drama performance art with origins in the Krishna-centered Vaishnavism monasteries of Assam and attributed to the 15th-century Bhakti movement scholar and saint Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev.
 
• Dance historian Dr. Sunil Kothari has recently been bestowed with the Madhabdev Award by the Government of Assam for popularising Sattriya dance.
 
• Sattriya was given the status of classical dance in the year 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
